pull.title: build: ci/doc win64-cross build via nix
pull.body:
Release cross-builds to win64 are done in guix. There are also docs to use Debian/Ubuntu for those cross-builds and this approach is used in CI. However, there are many problems:

* The CI is intended to mirror the guix build, but often it is not possible to find the major versions used for mingw and GCC in the guix build in the `apt` packages for an LTS distro.
* Users on older distro releases may lack released bugfixes, such as https://github.com/mingw-w64/mingw-w64/commit/8e06daa36dfcea4bb491acf4b350658f40738f02 in mingw 13  (e.g. Debian Trixie with mingw 12, https://packages.debian.org/trixie/mingw-w64-x86-64-dev).
* When using the UCRT variant of the build, this uncovers bugs such as https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/mingw-w64/+bug/2106420 or https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=1121403.

So add a way to use nix to do the cross build. This allows to closer mimic the guix build.

Also, clarify that cygwin/msys2 are not tested/supported.

reACK fa8762da626a592585f936b9398a100e3adfd923
Also tested this on aarch64, so I think the three Debian/Ubuntu bugs listed in OP are fixed/worked-around by this.

> Also tested this on aarch64, so I think the three Debian/Ubuntu bugs listed in OP are fixed/worked-around by this.

Additionally, this fixes https://qt-project.atlassian.net/browse/QTBUG-144294, which paves the way for updating Qt in depends.

> Additionally, this fixes https://qt-project.atlassian.net/browse/QTBUG-144294

Can you explain how this is fixed (by Nix)? What is the difference between the Ubuntu / Debian builds? (Also not clear how this unblocks updating Qt, unless you're also planning to drop support for building on Debian/Ubuntu entirely, and making Nix the only supported way to cross compile for Windows?)

> > Additionally, this fixes https://qt-project.atlassian.net/browse/QTBUG-144294
> 
> Can you explain how this is fixed (by Nix)?

No. I haven't bisected the toolchain changes.

> What is the difference between the Ubuntu / Debian builds?

On the master branch, configure summary reads:
```
C++ compiler .......................... GNU 14.0.0, /bin/x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++-posix
```

With this branch:
```
C++ compiler .......................... GNU 14.3.0, /nix/store/j1v9zdbf0l4qfvwybb90qwzyh1lmxfw1-x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc-wrapper-14.3.0/bin/x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++
```

> (Also not clear how this unblocks updating Qt, unless you're also planning to drop support for building on Debian/Ubuntu entirely, and making Nix the only supported way to cross compile for Windows?)

Debian / Ubuntu might update their packages in the future.
Ah ok. So (probably?) a fix in a GCC point release, and the unblocking is unrelated to Nix.

It could also be a fix in mingw? Ubuntu 24.04 ships with mingw-11.

Of course Nix doesn't fix the bugs in Ubuntu/Debian, but allowing to side-step them with Nix should be a good enough "fix" for us.

There was plenty of time for anyone to fix them in Ubuntu/Debian, but given that no one has done so, it seems time to give up on that. Of course, no one is holding anyone back from porting fixes to Ubuntu/Debian, and it would be trivial to switch back. Though, for now, I think it is a better use of time to just focus on shipping bug-free binaries with guix (and offering a working equivalent toolchain via nix on Ubuntu/Debian/etc)

> It could also be a fix in mingw? Ubuntu 24.04 ships with mingw-11.

https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36029 proposes logging the MinGW-w64 version in the configure summary to help track things like this.

> It could also be a fix in mingw?

From https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34578#issuecomment-5353146775:
> My guess is that the issue was fixed in [mingw-w64/mingw-w64@8e06daa](https://github.com/mingw-w64/mingw-w64/commit/8e06daa36dfcea4bb491acf4b350658f40738f02).
Thx. That bug is already mentioned in the OP here, and one of the reasons for this pull.

These should be caught in the docker buildkit layer cache naively, but any miss there in base_install.sh or earlier will cause a rebuild of the above, I think.

We may therefore want to consider a combination of pinning the nixpkgs commit, and using [cachix](https://github.com/cachix/cachix) ([docs](https://nix.dev/guides/recipes/continuous-integration-github-actions)) or similar to cache built packages on pushes to master.

Noting that this is another "account" for someone to manage and another repo `secret` needed, but probably worth it IMO. The cachix cache woudl also be readable for developers to use themselves, if they add the cachix cache alongside cache.nixos.org

Also noting that this adds 1.9GB to the docker image as configured.

Finally, it is possible that these do get cached on cache.nixos.org (I just don't know how to check), but the hydra server which builds them [lags behind](https://hydra.nixos.org/queue-summary). I suspect these aren't being built though, as building all cross-combinations would be too expensive.

Hmm, I think storage is cheap, so I think this is good enough for now. Also, I probably won't be able to run a cachix for this, but maybe foo.fish can, if other reviewers think it is overall worth it?

But I think for now it seems fine to eat the 1.9 GB twice.

Yeah, a pin makes sense here. Especially if this is ever switched to the `unstable` channel in the future, a pin would be even be required then.

Ok so I've been invesitgating this more, and I don't think it's worth havnig any more cache than the docker buildkit layer caching here.

We _can_ add [one](https://cache.nix.fish.foo/index.html), but the machinery detailing when to use it, when to be read vs write, how to mount into the container etc. is probably not worth it IMO.

The downside is that a cache miss on that buildkit layer now takes 30 mins longer to rebuild all the nix packages...

Perhaps I'll revisit the idea in the future if this turns up too frequently and is bothersome.
